coverage: Holiday edition, Thu Nov 26. US markets closed for Thanksgiving. Covers the Wed Nov 25 session and news since.
moodReason: A hot October PCE report pushed a December Fed rate hike to near certainty, and new tariff proposals and an AI and tech sell-off hit stocks on Wednesday. The Dow's late recovery kept the index losses small, but the S&P 500 and Nasdaq still closed lower.

stories.headline: October PCE inflation rises to 3.8% and a December Fed hike is nearly priced in
stories.what: The Bureau of Economic Analysis reported headline PCE inflation of 3.8% year over year for October, up from 3.6% in September. Core PCE rose to 3.3%, above the 3.2% forecast and the highest level in three years.
stories.why: Hot inflation keeps the Fed on track to raise rates at its Dec 8 to 9 meeting, with CME FedWatch odds of roughly 94% to 98%. Higher rates raise borrowing costs and weigh on high-valuation stocks.

stories.headline: Trump proposes new tariffs on 14 trading partners, with China at 20%
stories.what: The administration proposed tariffs on 14 trading partners, aimed at excess factory capacity. Proposed rates include 15% for the EU, Japan and South Korea and 20% for China. Mexico and Norway are excluded while their investigations continue. The rates would not take effect until after a Jan 25 public hearing.
stories.why: New tariffs raise import costs and could keep inflation and interest rates elevated. Global stocks fell on the news, with MSCI's world gauge down about 0.5%. Some analysts see the rates as opening bargaining positions, which could limit the damage if talks succeed.

stories.headline: AI and tech stocks sell off sharply before recovering, with Nvidia down 3.9%
stories.what: The Nasdaq fell as much as 4.6% intraday and the S&P 500 as much as 3.2% before recovering. Nvidia closed 3.9% lower at $149.30 despite a Q3 revenue report of $115.8 billion, its first report without Jensen Huang as CEO. Micron and Sandisk also fell. Meta and Salesforce rose.
stories.why: The AI leaders carry a large share of index weight, so their sell-off drags on the S&P 500 and Nasdaq. Investors are questioning whether strong results justify valuations while Nvidia has interim leadership and rising policy risks.

stories.headline: Treasury yields ease as the 10-year falls to about 4.86%
stories.what: The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 7 basis points to around 4.86% on Wednesday, while the 30-year was near 5.24%. Yields had been high in recent weeks on Fed hike bets.
stories.why: Lower yields ease pressure on stock valuations, but the 30-year remains above 5%. Yields could move quickly again once traders react to the PCE data and the December Fed decision.

stories.headline: Breadth improves as small caps outperform, though most of the S&P 500 rose
stories.what: About three quarters of S&P 500 stocks rose on Wednesday, and the Russell 2000 gained about 0.7% to 2,704.06. Heavy technology weighting kept the S&P 500 down 0.25%.
stories.why: Broader participation suggests the sell-off was concentrated in a few large AI names. Small caps are more sensitive to borrowing costs, so their strength is a mixed signal while rate hike bets persist.

stories.headline: Oil climbs about 2.5% as the US and Iran conflict remains unresolved
stories.what: WTI crude rose to roughly $84 per barrel, up about 2.5% on Wednesday. Coverage tied oil prices to the unresolved US and Iran conflict.
stories.why: Higher oil feeds into headline inflation, which is already running near 4%. That reinforces the case for further Fed tightening.

watch.item: Early stock market close at 1:00 p.m. ET after the Thanksgiving holiday
Fed policy meeting, where a 25 basis point rate hike is widely expected
Next PCE inflation release, after the December Fed meeting
Public hearing on the proposed tariffs on 14 trading partners

bottomLine: Inflation is running hot, with headline PCE at 3.8% and core at 3.3%, and markets now expect the Fed to raise rates again in December. New tariff proposals add to the inflation risk and to uncertainty for global trade. The AI sell-off showed that the market's leaders are vulnerable, though the Dow's recovery and broader gains suggest investors have not abandoned stocks yet. Trading resumes Friday on a shortened session.
